feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. Iteration 3 (328.4) showed that narrowing wheel_track from 0.10 to 0.09 m, on the iteration 1 array, raised s-bend progress from 0.236 to 0.446 and tightened oval tracking (rms 0.0146, max_error 0.038), but oval finishes fell from 17 to 13. Slalom progress stayed at 0.17 and max_error stayed near 0.06 to 0.069, so turn authority does not explain the slalom failure. Iteration 2 showed that a wider array (±0.06 m, 7 sensors) raised oscillation from 0.20 to 0.37 and cut oval finishes to 4 of 20, so widening the span is not the fix. Iterations 0 and 1 both show line_loss_events of about 1.0 per run on bends, so the robot reacts late rather than turning too weakly. This candidate tests lookahead by moving the row forward. Next race: if slalom progress rises above 0.25 and steering_oscillation stays near 0.2 on the oval, keep y=0.08 m and try wheel_radius next. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3, return the row to y=0.07 m, since the extra lag is the likely cause. If the oval finishes stay below 13 of 20 with no slalom gain, return wheel_track to 0.10 m, because the narrower track costs oval stability.
requested_changes: If slalom progress rises above 0.25 and steering_oscillation on the oval stays near 0.2, keep sensor_positions at y=0.08 m and test wheel_radius 0.04 m (iteration 1 and 3 mean oval finish time was about 1.72 s, so extra ground speed has room to help).

If steering_oscillation on the oval rises above about 0.3 (iteration 2 reached 0.37 with a wider array), move sensor_positions y back to 0.07 m and keep wheel_track at 0.09 m, since iteration 3 showed that track width helped s-bend progress without raising oscillation.
If oval finishes fall below 13 of 20 with no slalom gain, set wheel_track back to 0.10 m, the iteration 1 value that gave 17 of 20 finishes, and keep sensor_positions at y=0.08 m.
